Company revenue grew 19.1%, operating margin reached 32.6%, and the company has now beaten consensus adjusted earnings in five consecutive quarters by 4.4% to 10.8%. Return on invested capital is 17.4%, net leverage is 0.88x, interest coverage is 15.4x, and cash rose from $742 million to $2,435 million in a single quarter. Nothing is wrong with this company. What is wrong is the price. At $288.20 the stock sits 0.37% below its all-time high after rising 56.4% in twelve months against the S&P 500's 24.3%, and it trades at 69.8x trailing adjusted earnings, 47.5x the 2027 consensus, 13.6x sales, 46.2x enterprise value to EBITDA, and 80.4x free cash flow — a free-cash-flow yield of 1.24%, the lowest in this batch by a factor of two. The street agrees the run is largely done: consensus of $299.18 is 3.8% above spot, the tightest implied upside of any name here. Our base fair value of $287 is 0.4% BELOW the close. IBKR.strategic_line: "Interactive Brokers closed 2026-08-04 at $88.63, 9.0% below its 52-week high with a relative strength index of 34.2 — oversold — two weeks after a quarter in which total net revenues rose 28.1% to $1.896 billion, diluted earnings per share rose 35.3% to $0.69, and the pre-tax profit margin went from 75% to 77%. The vendor file describes a different company in two specific ways. First, `inc_a.revenue` of $10,232 million for 2025 is a GROSS-UP that Interactive Brokers never publishes: the company's own top line is 'total net revenues' of $6,120 million, and `est.revenueAvg` for the same year is $6,121.7 million — an exact match to the net figure, so the estimate block and the income statement are 70% apart on a definition the file never labels. This is the SCHW defect, confirmed and quantified. Second, the market capitalisation of $153.156 billion divides by $88.63 to imply 1,728.0 million shares — but the 10-Q states that Interactive Brokers Group, Inc. owns approximately 26.3% of IBG LLC through 445,616,326 membership interests, with IBG Holdings LLC holding 1,250,737,416, for a total of 1,696,353,742. The price-to-earnings ratio survives that mismatch by accident; price-to-sales at 13.79x does not, because it divides a fully-exchanged market capitalisation by gross-up revenue and is wrong twice over. Our knowledge base is the strongest bullish lane in this batch — 16 claims, zero bearish — but it fails its own concentration test in an instructive way: nine of the sixteen come from a single episode of one show recorded on 2025-05-17, one carries the speaker_role 'management' and is Thomas Peterffy himself, and one carries an explicit test — 'IBKR breaks $100' — that has NOT been met. Base fair value $99, 11.7% above spot and 8.1% below the street's $107.75, where the lowest of 19 targets sits above the price. Buy — Tactical."

IBM.strategic_line: "IBM is the most genuinely two-sided name in this batch and the one where the vendor file is most wrong. The bull case is real: Software is now $29.962B and 44% of revenue at a 32.2% segment margin, free cash flow was $11.575B on $1.617B of capital expenditure, and the company has paid a dividend every year since 1916. The bear case is equally real and it arrived in the June quarter: total revenue grew 0.6% on the segment basis, IBM Z fell 42%, Consulting grew 0.2%, and the chief financial officer said the company 'faced revenue headwinds late in the second quarter'. The stock is down 28.6% from its 52-week high of $329.23 and 25.3% over six months while the S&P rose 11.1%. Three data-integrity findings matter. First, the vendor's total debt of $67.154B at 2025-12-31 is $5.894B above the 10-Q's $61,260M, and the mechanism is exact: the vendor counts $3,347M of operating-lease liabilities as debt and then counts the $2,547M non-current portion of them a SECOND time in `capitalLeaseObligations`. Second, the balance sheet predates the $11.5B Confluent acquisition that closed 2026-03-17 and took cash from $14.5B to $8.2B. Third, FY2025 GAAP net income of $10.593B exceeded pre-tax income of $10.328B because the tax provision was NEGATIVE $242M — roughly $1.3B of the Q4 2025 result was a discrete tax item that has not repeated, and the 2026 quarters carry positive provisions of $313M and $484M. Our base fair value of $250 is 6.3% above spot and 2.3% below the street. The knowledge base has the deepest lane in this batch, 23 entity hits, and the most attribution problems: three claims about IBM's own strategy are filed under a channel named for a different company's chief executive. Watch."

ICE.strategic_line: "Six days before this dive, on 29 July 2026, Intercontinental Exchange agreed to acquire MarketAxess Holdings for $167.00 per share in CASH, backstopped by a $6.25 billion 364-day senior unsecured bridge facility from Bank of America. That transaction appears in no vendor field, the earnings-release exhibits are not in the extraction, and the company has published no accretion arithmetic this archive can reach — so the largest capital commitment ICE has made since the $10.2 billion Black Knight purchase in 2023 is, from this file, an unquantified event. It lands on a stock that has already fallen 20.8% from its 52-week high and underperformed the S&P by 43 points over twelve months, the worst relative record in this batch. The arithmetic underneath is genuinely attractive: 17.0x the FY2027 consensus of $8.78, a 52.0% EBITDA margin, a 44.9% operating margin, a 5.79% free-cash-flow yield, and a street that is 33 positive out of 36 with a LOW price target of $163 that is 9.2% above spot. Our base fair value of $165 is 10.6% above spot and the asymmetry is 2.19:1, which does clear the bar. We are declining the Buy tier anyway and saying why: the acquisition is six days old and unquantified here, second-quarter net revenue growth decelerated to 4.8% from 20.6% in the March quarter, the first half contains a $452 million gain on investments the payload does not flag, and the only recent knowledge-base claim on this name argues at conviction 85 that guaranteed-settlement clearing 'can't compete' with the perpetuals model — a claim tagged BULLISH whose content is structurally bearish for ICE, which is the documented stance-inversion defect appearing on a second exchange after CME."

ILMN.verdict: Watch — do not chase, and trim into strength if held. The operational turnaround is real and complete (operating income swung from −$833M in FY24 to +$864M in FY25; free cash flow $931M), but revenue has now declined for four consecutive years while the stock has risen 92.9% in twelve months, and at $198.16 it trades ABOVE the street's own $181.18 consensus target with 24 of 50 raters at Hold or Sell. ILMN.strategic_line: Illumina is the reference case for a business whose price fixed itself faster than its revenue did. The margin repair is genuine and should not be dismissed — FY24 operating income of −$833M became +$864M in FY25, gross margin went from 60.9% (FY23) to 66.8% trailing, R&D intensity fell from 30.1% of revenue to 21.3%, and the company converted that into $1,079M of operating cash flow, $931M of free cash flow and $742M of buybacks. But strip the P&L repair away and look at the top line: $4,584M (FY22) → $4,504M (FY23) → $4,372M (FY24) → $4,338M (FY25). Four straight annual declines, a cumulative −5.4%, in the company that is supposed to be the picks-and-shovels supplier to a genomics boom. Consensus does not model a recovery so much as a stabilisation: +6.2% (FY26E), +5.8% (FY27E), +6.9% (FY28E). China revenue has halved from $502M (FY21) to $243M (FY25), a five-year continuous decline that is visible in the file and is the clearest evidence that this is a contested franchise, not a monopoly. Against that, the stock is +92.9% over twelve months and +45.9% over three, trades at 33.0x FY27E EPS for a mid-single-digit revenue grower, and sits above the consensus target with the sell-side already split 26 positive / 24 neutral-or-negative. You are being asked to pay a growth multiple for a cost-cutting story that has finished cutting. Watch.

INTC.strategic_line: "Intel's reported numbers are unusable in both directions at once, and almost nobody is doing the work to see it. The Q2'26 headline was a GAAP net loss of $11.033B, or minus $2.16 a share, on operating income of PLUS $1.981B. The bridge is a single line in the 10-Q - a $12.5B non-cash loss on the change in fair value of the derivative liability for the shares Intel issued into escrow for the U.S. government, driven, in the filing's own words, \"by an increase in our stock price.\" The liability was $2.7B at 2025-12-27 and $15.6B at 2026-06-27. Intel now books a multi-billion-dollar accounting loss every time its own shares rise. Screens therefore show a company at minus 47.8x trailing earnings with a minus 10.8% return on equity, which is noise. Strip it out and the operating business is genuinely better than it has been in three years - Q2'26 revenue $16.1B, up 25.5% year over year, Data Center and AI up 59%, Intel Products operating income $4.8B in the quarter, and a non-GAAP result of $0.42 against a $0.21 estimate. But strip it out and the valuation is also far worse than it looks, because 8.93x trailing sales and 5.89x book on a company earning nothing is what you are actually paying. The number that settles it is Intel Foundry. It lost $2.1B in Q2'26 and $4.5B in the first half. The 10-Q attributes $1.8B of the year-on-year improvement to lower period charges and simultaneously discloses $830M of LOWER product profit - so on an underlying basis the foundry deteriorated. Its genuinely third-party revenue is at most about $112M a quarter, once Altera, a business Intel itself sold last September, is removed from the $293M external line. The January 10-K states it flatly - \"we have been unsuccessful to date in securing any significant external foundry customers for any of our nodes.\" Back out a fair value for Intel Products and the market is currently ascribing roughly $258B - half the share price - to that foundry. At $100.94, after a 422.7% twelve-month run and a 10.92% single session, the price is the bull case."

INTU.strategic_line: "Intuit has lost 58.3% of its value in twelve months while its revenue grew 14.0% and its earnings per share grew roughly 19%, and that gap is the entire investment question. At $323.60 the shares are 58.8% below the 52-week high of $784.87 — the deepest drawdown in this batch by a factor of four — and trade at 13.6x the fiscal 2026 consensus of $23.83 and 11.8x fiscal 2027's $27.38, with a free-cash-flow yield of 8.64% and net debt of roughly $2.2 billion against $18.8 billion of annual revenue. The filed numbers show no deterioration whatsoever: nine-month fiscal 2026 revenue of $17,094 million against $15,000 million, up 14.0%, with the April quarter at $8,558 million against $7,754 million and adjusted earnings per share of $12.80 against a $12.57 estimate. The market is not pricing the past; it is pricing generative artificial intelligence dissolving consumer tax preparation and small-business bookkeeping. The knowledge base contains that argument in its sharpest available form and the counter-argument in its most specific: arthur_hayes, 2026-03-24, bearish 70 at the highest skill weight in the lane, says SaaS darlings in tax and accounting software get gutted as AI does the same work at roughly 1% cost, with collapsing recurring revenue making their leverage unserviceable; a16z, 2026-03-06, speaker Alex, bullish 58, says nobody is getting rid of QuickBooks because small-business owners log in directly so the front end IS the back end, and that TurboTax's edge is asking the right questions rather than knowing the published tax code. On 2026-05-20 Intuit announced a 17% reduction in its full-time workforce with $300-340 million of charges, and on 2026-05-07 the board authorised an additional $8 billion of buyback — roughly 11% of the market capitalisation including the balance. Neither appears in the payload. Our base fair value of $383 is 18.4% above spot with 1.65:1 asymmetry, and the honest caveat is that this distribution is BIMODAL rather than continuous: a probability-weighted midpoint describes no world anyone will actually inhabit. Fiscal fourth-quarter results and the first fiscal 2027 guidance arrive 2026-08-25, twenty-one days from now, and that is the event."

Over twelve months the shares have returned MINUS 23.8% against the S&P 500's plus 24.3% — a 48-point deficit — leaving them 37.9% below a 52-week high of $592.85, below both moving averages, with the 200-day sitting 23.5% overhead. Worldwide da Vinci procedures grew approximately 15% in the June quarter — against approximately 17% a year earlier — with United States procedures at 12% and outside the United States at 20%. That deceleration, from a starting multiple somewhere north of 60 times forward earnings, is the entire explanation for the de-rating. What is left is a business where 75.4% of revenue is instruments, accessories and services sold into an installed base that only ratchets upward, gross margin is 66.7%, there is no meaningful debt and roughly $9.2 billion of cash and investments, and the company repurchased $2,295 million of stock in FY2025 — its first large buyback since 2022. At $368.265 the stock trades at 30.5 times the FY2027 consensus of $12.08, against a street target of $491.15 that implies 33.4% upside and against five sell ratings, the most in this batch. Our base fair value of $399 is 8.3% above spot and 18.8% below the street's. The knowledge base returns six hits of which three come from a channel that IS the company's management — the only such lane in this batch — and one is a homograph on Intuitive Machines, a lunar-lander business. Our base fair value of $270 is 8.5% below spot and the payoff ratio is 0.51:1, the worst in the batch. Two data findings. The filing extraction is PROSE-ONLY — zero table markers in either the 10-K or the 10-Q — AND the archive contains no June-quarter 10-Q at all, only the September 2025 and March 2026 filings, so the capital-expenditure check could not be performed and no second-quarter statement could be verified. And `seg_geo` for FY2025 sums to 152.9% of revenue because the block carries a North America aggregate of $8,480 million alongside its own two components, United States $7,395 million and Other North America $1,085 million, which sum to $8,480 million exactly — the CDNS/CSX over-count class, and the first year in which a United States line appears at all."

JNJ.strategic_line: "Johnson & Johnson has quietly been one of the best large-cap holdings of the last twelve months — up 52.4% against SPY's 24.3%, a 28-point outperformance that almost nobody frames as a growth story because it is not one. Revenue grew 6.0% in fiscal 2025 and 5.6% operationally in the June quarter. What re-rated was not the earnings, it was the discount: the market has spent a decade valuing J&J with a talc-shaped hole in it, and on 2026-07-28 the Company filed an 8-K announcing a comprehensive resolution of the ovarian talc litigation with the MDL and state-court leadership — a $5.5 billion commitment, first payment of no more than $3 billion in 2027, nothing further before 2028, conditioned on at least 95% of remaining claims participating. That is the re-rating. Three things follow, and all three argue that the good news is now in the price. First, the $5.5B commitment exceeds the $3.7B present-value reserve the 10-Q carries, so a top-up charge is arithmetically likely; and the 95% participation condition is not yet satisfied. Second, on 2026-07-29 — the very next day — J&J closed Firefly Bio and signed a Sail Biomedicines collaboration that it says will reduce 2026 adjusted EPS by about $0.64 and 2027 adjusted EPS by about $1.36, the latter being 10.6% of the vendor's FY2027 consensus of $12.875, and we cannot confirm from this file that consensus has absorbed it. Third, on 2026-08-04 — today — a third 8-K disclosed that the Executive Vice President and Worldwide Chairman of Innovative Medicine, the segment that is 64% of revenue, retires on 1 September. Three 8-Ks in eight days is not a coincidence; it is a company in transition. Underneath, the fundamentals are genuinely good: oncology grew 22.1% in 2025 and 16.1% operationally in the first half of 2026, Stelara's biosimilar drag is easing from 6.2% of worldwide operational sales in 2025 to 4.6% in the June quarter, the balance sheet carries $27.8 billion of net debt against $24.5 billion of annual operating cash flow, and the dividend has risen for 63 consecutive years. But at $254.93 the stock trades at 19.8x FY2027 consensus adjusted EPS against a decade in the mid-teens, the street is 16 hold and 3 sell with a low target of $255 — essentially at spot — and our base fair value of $270 is only 5.9% above. Own it for the yield and the quality. Do not chase the re-rating."

JPM.strategic_line: "The headline is that JPMorgan beat the second-quarter estimate by 36% — $7.59 against $5.59. The arithmetic says essentially all of that beat was a single non-operating item, and the Firm told us it was coming. The Q1'26 10-Q, filed 2026-05-01, disclosed under Recent events that JPMorgan had tendered its 18.6 million Visa Class B-2 shares into an exchange offer, that those shares are carried at nominal basis, and that the Visa Class C shares received would be recognised at fair value, producing a gain that may be recorded as early as the second quarter of 2026. The payload then shows precisely that shape: net interest income essentially flat quarter-on-quarter ($25.366B to $25.511B, +0.6%), the provision essentially flat ($2.507B to $2.515B — so this was NOT a reserve release), the tax rate normal at 23.1%, and noninterest revenue jumping $7.366B, from $24.470B to $31.836B, a 30% step in three months. Tax-effect that step and it is roughly $2.05 a share. Subtract it and the quarter earned about $5.50-5.60 against a $5.59 estimate — in line, not a 36% beat. This is not a hypothesis about an unnamed item: the Firm booked a structurally identical $7.9B Visa gain in Q2'24, and its own 2025 Form 10-K attributes the FY2025 noninterest-revenue softness to the absence of that gain. Strip the noise and what is left is a superb bank at a full price. Filed FY2025 return on tangible common equity was 20%; Q1'26 was 23%. Filed tangible book value per share was $107.56 at 2025-12-31 and $108.87 at 2026-03-31, compounding 8-10.5%. At $357.52 the stock trades at roughly 3.2x a derived Q2'26 tangible book of about $112 — and a residual-income frame, justified price-to-tangible-book equals (ROTCE minus growth) divided by (cost of equity minus growth), says that multiple already requires a sustained ROTCE of about 21%. The Firm is earning 20-21%. There is no discount to harvest, the base case is $372 against a street consensus of $367.83, and the skew is negative: 18% up to the bull, 23% down to the bear. Hold."

The vendor's fiscal-2025 balance sheet reports cash of $6.155 MILLION where the prior year showed $14,878 million. KLAC.strategic_line: "This dive replaces an earlier 2026-08-04 KLAC dive written against a truncated SEC archive. The complete archive contains the single fact that reframes every share-count, dividend and per-share figure in the file: KLA executed a TEN-FOR-ONE forward stock split effective 11:59pm Eastern on 2026-06-11, first traded split-adjusted 2026-06-12, with authorised shares raised from 500,000,000 to 5,000,000,000 — and in the same 2026-05-07 announcement raised the quarterly dividend 21% to $2.30 pre-split, guiding the August 2026 declaration to $0.23 post-split. The earlier archive carried the split-effecting 8-K but not the announcement that explains it. On the business: fiscal 2026 (year ended 2026-06-30) delivered revenue of $13,579.5M (+11.7%), a 61.30% gross margin, a 41.69% operating margin and GAAP diluted EPS of $3.66 — but those annual figures are UNAUDITED and press-release-derived; the FY2026 10-K is not yet filed and the earnings release itself is NOT in this archive, so the latest filing-verified financials stop at the March 2026 quarter. At $195.45 — up 6.95% today and still 35.2% below the 52-week high of $301.71 after a 120.4% twelve-month run — KLA trades at 53.4x trailing GAAP earnings, 35.6x the FY2027 consensus of $5.483 and 29.5x FY2028's $6.625, on a free cash flow yield of 1.48% computed as filed operating cash flow minus filed capital expenditure. Consensus wants FY2027 revenue of $17,985M, a 32.4% increase, against a Q1 FY2027 revenue estimate of $4,038M that annualises to $16,152M. Our base of $205 is 4.9% above spot with 1.44:1 asymmetry, which does not clear the bar. Three genuinely clean data findings are recorded — capital expenditure verified against three filed years, seg_geo and seg_prod both tying to reported revenue to the dollar with the home market present — alongside four defects, including an EBITDA fabrication signature fixed at exactly 42.51% of revenue in every forward year and a split-adjustment inconsistency inside the estimate array itself."

KMI.strategic_line: "Kinder Morgan owns 66,000 miles of natural-gas pipeline and moves roughly 40% of the natural gas consumed in the United States, and it has just delivered two consecutive quarters that beat consensus by 21.3% and 15.4% while its shares fell 3.4% over the same three months. The Natural Gas Pipelines segment took revenue from $8,942 million in 2024 to $11,009 million in 2025, up 23.1%, on the demand nobody disputes: liquefied-natural-gas export terminals, power generation and data centres. And yet the consensus estimate row is the most striking thing in this file — FY2026 EPS of $1.516 followed by FY2027 EPS of $1.527, growth of 0.8%, on ten analysts. The street is telling you that after the LNG build finishes arriving, this is a flat business. At $31.38 that is 20.7x FY2026 and 20.5x FY2027, on a 3.76% dividend the company has guided to grow 2% next year, against a balance sheet carrying $32,248 million of debt at 4.0x trailing EBITDA and a $3,059 million working-capital deficit. On 2026-07-28 Kinder Morgan priced $1.75 billion of new senior notes at 5.550% and 6.150% — coupons that settle on 2026-08-06, two days after this dive, and which appear nowhere in the vendor payload. Neither does the $503 million Monument Pipeline acquisition completed on 2026-05-01, nor the revolving credit facility amended on 2026-05-21 to extend maturity from 2026 to 2031. And the entire SEC archive for this name is PROSE-ONLY — zero preserved table markers across the 10-K and both 10-Qs — so the balance-sheet and cash-flow verification this programme normally performs could not be run, and every figure that could not be checked is labelled. Our base fair value of $34 is 8.4% above spot with a 3.76% dividend on top. That is a decent income return and it is not a Buy."

KO.strategic_line: "This dive replaces an earlier 2026-08-04 KO dive written against a truncated SEC archive in which, in that dive's own words, all of the 8-Ks were 'present as XBRL cover-page tags only.' The complete archive carries their full Item content, and two of them are material and are absent from the vendor payload entirely. FIRST: on 2026-07-16 — nineteen days before this dive — Coca-Cola disclosed that fairlife, LLC, its wholly-owned dairy business, suffered a ransomware event and that 'production operations at fairlife in the United States are temporarily suspended,' with the company stating plainly that 'the full scope, nature and impacts of the incident are not yet known' and that it 'has not yet determined whether the incident is reasonably likely to materially affect the Company.' fairlife is the asset for which Coca-Cola paid a $6,173 million final contingent-consideration milestone in March 2025 — a payment large enough on its own to drive fiscal 2025 operating cash flow down to $7,408 million. SECOND: on 2026-06-25 the company announced that Jennifer Mann, President of the North America operating unit — 40.4% of second-quarter revenue — departs 2026-07-31, and that John Murphy, President and Chief Financial Officer, assumes North America on an interim basis from 2026-08-01, four days before this dive. Underneath the events the business is performing well: second-quarter revenue of $13,380 million (+6.7%), worldwide unit case volume +5%, an operating margin of 34.9% against 28.7% for fiscal 2025, and six-month free cash flow of $6,859 million on filed numbers. At $86.56 — 2.8% below the 52-week high — that is 26.0x trailing earnings, 24.5x the FY2027 consensus of $3.532 and a 3.84% trailing free cash flow yield, for 7% earnings growth and a 2.45% forward dividend. Base fair value $88, 1.7% above spot, asymmetry 1.22:1. The knowledge base's single most on-point claim, from compound_and_friends on 2025-10-03, is that the stock 'is priced for its next decade of growth and may be flat in 10 years,' and nothing in this arithmetic contradicts it."

LIN.strategic_line: "Linde is the highest-quality industrial-gas franchise in the world attached, on 2026-08-04, to a price that still pays a growth multiple for a mid-single-digit-growth business. The quality is not rhetorical: on-site supply contracts run 10-20 years with minimum-purchase and price-escalation clauses, the 10-Q puts remaining performance obligations at approximately $64 billion with contract durations of up to thirty years, and reported operating profit has risen every year since 2020 — $3.889B, $5.283B, $6.460B, $8.105B, $8.595B, $8.923B. The company has grown adjusted EPS at roughly 10% a year while revenue grew about 5%, and it did so with a 0.723 beta. The problem is that at $484.64 the stock trades at 28.1x trailing adjusted EPS of $17.24 and 27.1x the FY2026 consensus of $17.895, for a business consensus expects to grow revenue 6.4%, 4.9% and 5.6% over the next three years. LITE.strategic_line: "Lumentum has returned 696.3% over twelve months, rose 8.92% on the day this dive was struck, and reported net revenue for the quarter ended 2026-03-28 up 90.1% year on year - a $383.2 million increase driven by $232.5 million of Components and $150.7 million of Systems growth. The filing is specific about what is inside those numbers, and the specificity is what makes this file interesting: laser chip and laser assembly shipments ramping across intra-data-centre, data-centre-interconnect and long-haul applications with average selling prices RISING on a shift to 200G lane speeds; cloud transceiver revenue up more than $137.0 million in the quarter and $268.0 million across nine months; and optical circuit switches - an entirely new product category - contributing more than $25.0 million in the quarter and $38.0 million across nine months, with the company describing itself as on track for manufacturing expansion. Consensus carries revenue from $1,645 million in the year to June 2025 to $3,001 million, $5,673 million and $8,772 million across the three years to June 2028. The knowledge base has three claims on this name, all bullish, all within five months, from three independent channels and two named speakers, and every one identifies the same mechanism: optical interconnect is a physical choke point in AI infrastructure. Against all of that stand four numbers. The stock trades at 45.7 times the FY2027 consensus and 103.3 times FY2026. Two customers individually accounted for 26% and 12% of revenue in the March quarter. The company is running an active convertible-note conversion machine - $1,265.0 million of 0.375% 2032 Notes issued 2025-09-08 at a conversion price of approximately $187.77 against a share price of $849.47, $500.8 million of early conversion requests outstanding at 2026-04-30, and 5.7 million shares issued on 2026-04-07 alone in privately negotiated exchanges, which is 7.3% of the 77.8 million shares outstanding. And fourth-quarter results land on 2026-08-11, seven days from now. Our base of $1,000 is 17.7% above spot with 1.58:1 asymmetry against a street consensus of $1,082.67 whose lowest constituent is already above the price. This is the best business in this batch and the entry is the worst-timed. Watch, with upgrade conditions that resolve on 2026-08-11."

LLY.strategic_line: "Eli Lilly is the purest listed expression of the house anchor thesis — metabolic disease as the master switch of chronic illness — and it is running the fastest large-cap revenue growth in this batch: +45.2% in FY2025 to $65.179B, +55.5% year-over-year in the first quarter of 2026, at an 83.8% gross margin. It is also the most concentrated business we cover: the 10-Q states that Mounjaro and Zepbound alone were 65 percent of total revenue in the first quarter of 2026, up from 56 percent for the full year 2025. This dive is written into a specific and unusual moment. The company reports the second quarter TOMORROW, 2026-08-05, on consensus EPS of $6.06 and revenue of $20.685B, after FIVE consecutive large beats (the most recent $8.55 against $6.97). Two things about that streak deserve stating plainly. First, the consensus $6.06 is 4.0% BELOW the $6.31 the company earned in the same quarter last year, on revenue expected to rise 33% — an arithmetic that only resolves through large charges, most plausibly acquired in-process R&D from up to $12 billion of pending acquisitions the 10-Q discloses. Second, the last beat was lower quality than it looked: the 10-Q attributes part of it to a favorable ONE-TIME adjustment to estimates for rebates and discounts, the effective tax rate fell to 16.4% from 20.2%, and there was no repeat of the prior-year $1.57B in-process charge. The data in this file is a quarter stale — the newest income statement ends 2026-03-31. The technical setup is the opposite of stretched: RSI 42.1, MACD negative, 3.1% below the 50-DMA, 9.7% below the 52-week closing high. Base fair value $1,220 at 27.0x FY2027 consensus is 9.3% above spot and 7.3% BELOW the street's $1,315.42 — we are the more cautious party. Own it; do not complete the purchase into a print you cannot handicap."

LMT.strategic_line: "Lockheed Martin has just delivered the best backlog disclosure in its history and the most overbought technical reading in this batch at the same time, and our fair value lands BELOW the current price. Backlog at 28 June 2026 was $230.4 billion — 3.07x trailing revenue — up $36.8 billion in six months on an undefinitized contractual action for the THAAD programme, and international revenue has risen from 26.1% to 28.4% of the total with Europe up 14.1% and Asia Pacific up 25.2% year on year. The June quarter beat consensus earnings by 10.0% and grew revenue 10.5%. Against that sits a company that has recognised approximately $1.8 billion of cumulative reach-forward losses on one classified Aeronautics programme and approximately $1.5 billion on a classified programme at Missiles and Fire Control, that faces a securities class action filed 2025-07-28 alleging misstatements about exactly those programmes, that carries NEGATIVE tangible book value of $18.75 per share and a 2.34x debt-to-equity ratio, and that announced on 6 July 2026 a $3.45 billion acquisition of Ultra Maritime Solutions to be funded with 'cash on hand and additional financing arrangements' — a transaction that appears nowhere in the vendor payload. At $589.13 the stock trades at 21.6x trailing earnings and 18.1x the FY2027 consensus of $32.63, after a 40.0% twelve-month return against the S&P 500's 24.3%, with RSI at 81.0 — the most overbought reading in this batch by a wide margin. Watch."

LNG.verdict: Hold — the largest US LNG exporter, priced at 7.67x FY27E consensus EV/EBITDA with a base fair value of $273 (+5.8%) and earnings in two days (2026-08-06). Two things stop this from being a Buy despite an overwhelming 25-of-27 sell-side Buy consensus. First, the Q1'26 result carried roughly $5.5B of below-the-operating-line losses the dataset does not identify, producing GAAP EPS of -$16.65 against a +$4.25 consensus, and pushing FY26E consensus EPS to NEGATIVE $6.62 — you cannot underwrite this earnings series on GAAP. Second, the knowledge base's own highest-conviction gas voice argues US gas prices spike high enough to force shutting off export cargos, which is the specific mechanism that damages Cheniere's marketing margin. Wait for the print, and for a price nearer $225.
LNG.strategic_line: Cheniere is the toll booth on American gas leaving the country — two terminals (Sabine Pass in Cameron Parish, Louisiana and Corpus Christi, Texas), the 94-mile Creole Trail pipeline, the 21.5-mile Corpus Christi pipeline, and an LNG and natural-gas marketing business, run by 1,717 people generating $19.632B of FY25 revenue. The scale is remarkable: FY25 revenue up 24.4%, EBITDA $11.182B, operating income $5.304B, operating cash flow $5.539B, and a capital-return programme that retired $2.724B of stock plus $451M of dividends in FY25 alone — taking the diluted share count from 253.4M in FY22 to 210.5M by Q1'26, a 16.9% reduction. Twenty-seven analysts cover it with one strong buy, twenty-four buys, two holds and zero sells, at a $278.50 consensus target. And the demand backdrop is the strongest thematic signal in the entire knowledge base: invest_like_the_best (2026-07-21, conviction 82) describes a historic structural US gas deficit driven by LNG exports scaling from roughly 15 to 35 BCF/d plus AI compute. So why Hold? Because two specific things in the data refuse to resolve. The Q1'26 quarter produced positive, growing operating income of $1.973B (up 30.6% year over year) and a GAAP net loss of $3.502B — meaning roughly $5.5B of losses landed below the operating line, and this dataset does not identify what they were. That single quarter dragged FY26E consensus EPS to negative $6.62222. An earnings series that can swing $20 per share on an unexplained non-operating line is not one you can value on earnings, which is why this dive prices Cheniere on EV/EBITDA and says so. And the second thing is sharper: the same conviction-82 gas thesis that makes the demand case also carries an explicit warning — that prices could go high enough to force shutting off US export cargos — while compound_and_friends (2026-05-01, bearish, conviction 55) refuses to own Cheniere precisely because margins are a function of the gas price and management does not control its inputs. The tolling model is designed to neutralise exactly that risk. Whether it fully does is the open question, and the 2026-08-06 print is where you find out.

LOW.strategic_line: "Lowe's spent $10.1 billion of cash in fiscal 2025 buying two building-products distributors, and the reason it had to is that its own stores are not growing. Comparable sales were plus 0.2% for the full year and plus 0.6% in the quarter to 1 May 2026, and in both periods customer TRANSACTIONS fell — minus 2.8% and minus 0.9% — with the entire comp coming from a higher average ticket. Reported first-quarter revenue growth of 10.3% therefore contains 9.7 points of acquisition and 0.6 points of business. That is the whole picture in two numbers. The acquisitions themselves — Artisan Design Group for $1.3B in June 2025 and Foundation Building Materials for $8.8B in October 2025 — are a coherent strategic answer to a frozen housing market, moving Lowe's toward the professional contractor it does not serve well from a big box. But they were paid for with $2.0B of term loan at 4.661% and $5.0B of new notes, they took net debt to roughly $41.8 billion and net leverage to 3.4x EBITDA against a balance sheet whose book equity is MINUS $9.9 billion, and they increase rather than reduce exposure to new residential construction at a moment when the knowledge base's two freshest and highest-conviction housing claims — both conviction 80, one from March and one from July — say housing is frozen and that the weakness is demand, not rates. Against all of that: the stock is 24.1% below its 52-week high, 8.8% below its 200-day average, has underperformed the S&P 500 by 28 points over twelve months, yields 6.3% on free cash flow, and carries a street where all 51 analysts' price targets sit ABOVE the current price, the lowest at $232. Our base fair value of $235 is 7.8% above spot with a 2.25-to-1 upside skew. Good asymmetry, not enough base-case return, and second-quarter results land in fifteen days. Watch."

LPLA.verdict: Stage-In — the cheapest genuinely-growing business in this batch at 12.0x FY27 consensus earnings with a 0.507 beta, five consecutive quarterly beats, and a 26% expected EPS growth rate, but do not buy it all today with the RSI at 77.9 four sessions after a beat and the stock 4% off its high. Buy a third now, add on any pullback toward the 200-DMA.
LPLA.strategic_line: LPL is a scale-and-network business hiding inside a financial-services ticker, and the market is pricing it as a cyclical broker rather than the custody-and-platform utility it has become. The arithmetic is the argument: revenue has gone from $8.60B (FY22) to $16.99B (FY25), a 25% compound rate; adjusted earnings per share have gone $4.51, $5.20, $5.23, $5.60, $5.84 across the last five reported quarters — a straight line up, with the company beating the consensus EPS line in every one of them; and consensus models $23.69 (FY26E), $29.95 (FY27E) and $36.29 (FY28E), which at $360.35 is 15.2x, 12.0x and 9.9x. A business compounding earnings at roughly 26% for 10x forward earnings is unusual, and the beta of 0.507 says the market does not think it is a growth business at all. The catch is that you have to be honest about what you are buying. GAAP diluted earnings per share for FY25 were $10.92 against roughly $19.81 of adjusted earnings — a 45% gap — and the third quarter of 2025 printed an outright GAAP LOSS of -$0.37 while the adjusted line showed +$5.20. That gap is the Commonwealth acquisition, which cost $1.79B in FY25 on top of $1.02B in FY24 and pushed total debt to $7.26B against $5.34B of equity, with goodwill and intangibles of $5.98B leaving tangible book value NEGATIVE. Operating cash flow was minus $423M last year. This is a leveraged roll-up of financial-advisor practices being financed with debt, and the entire investment case rests on the acquisition charges being genuinely non-recurring so that GAAP converges up toward adjusted. If it does, the stock is worth $420. If the charges keep coming, you are paying 33x GAAP earnings for a levered balance sheet. Stage in, because the price is right and the timing is not.

LRCX.strategic_line: "Lam Research is the deposition-and-etch leg of wafer fabrication equipment and the most memory-levered of the four large WFE names. That is the whole case, and it is also the whole problem. Memory makers are in a genuine supercycle — Micron closed today at a $1.008 trillion market capitalisation with quarterly revenue up from $9.3B to $41.5B across five quarters — and memory profits convert into memory capital expenditure, which converts into Lam orders. But the conversion has been modest so far. Over the same five quarters Lam's revenue went from $4.720B to $6.722B, up 42%, against Micron's 4.5x. Lam's own 10-Q for the March 2026 quarter is explicit that the nine-month revenue increase was predominantly driven by Foundry equipment spending, with memory strengthening only in the most recent quarter. Meanwhile the equity has already been paid for the conversion twice over. Twelve months ago the stock was roughly $96 and trailing diluted earnings per share were $4.15, a 23.2x multiple. Today it is $317.74 on trailing diluted earnings per share of $5.76, a 55.2x multiple. Earnings rose 38.8%; the multiple rose 138%; the stock rose 229.7%. Roughly two-thirds of the twelve-month return was the market changing its mind, not the company changing its results. Consensus now models revenue of $34.573B in FY2027 (+48.8%) and diluted earnings per share of $11.77 by FY2028, and at $317.74 the price already pays 27.0x that FY2028 number — i.e. it assumes the memory capex wave lands in full AND that a cyclical equipment maker does not de-rate as its earnings peak. Both may happen. Neither is cheap. The balance sheet is genuinely clean (net cash of $1.845B, 66x interest coverage, 41.0% return on invested capital), and this is one of the very few names where the vendor's enterprise value is materially correct. But the capital-return story that used to carry the name has quietly become immaterial at this price — $3.851B of buyback plus $1.271B of dividends is a 1.29% shareholder yield on a $397B market capitalisation, and management's two most recent accelerated repurchases were struck at roughly $91 and roughly $219 a share, not $318. Every insider transaction in the file is a disposition, at $335 to $390. Deferred revenue has fallen from $2.77B at the September 2025 quarter to $2.22B at March 2026 on declining customer down payments. China is 37% of nine-month FY2026 revenue and rising. We do not have a variant perception on valuation — our base of $353 sits marginally below the street median of $355 — and by house rule a no-edge name defaults to Watch."

MA.strategic_line: "Mastercard is the mirror image of its twin on relative performance and very nearly its equal on price. The stock has returned 2.0% over twelve months against SPY's 24.3% — a twenty-two-point deficit, the widest relative underperformance in this batch — and then recovered 13.1% in three months against SPY's 7.6%, leaving it 4.7% below the 52-week closing high with RSI at 68.2 and, tellingly, a 50-day moving average ($517.02) that still sits BELOW the 200-day ($528.00). That is a name repairing a downtrend, not extending an uptrend. The business is better than the price action: value-added services and solutions is now 40.6% of net revenue, up from 35.4% in 2022, and grew 20% in the June quarter; operating margin expanded 330 basis points on an adjusted basis in 2025; and consensus models 16.0% annual EPS growth from FY2026 to FY2028 — 240 basis points faster than Visa. Three things the vendor cannot see. Total debt was $24.6 billion at 2026-06-30, not the $19.0 billion on the vendor's stale year-end sheet — the 10-Q says so, and the $5.6 billion increase funded a buyback that exceeded operating cash flow in the half. The vendor's own earnings calendar reports revenue of $9.277 billion for BOTH the June and March quarters, which is impossible; the filing and the quarterly income statements put March at $8.398 billion. And stockholders' equity of $7.737 billion against $83.2 billion of treasury stock makes book value, price-to-book (89.8x) and debt-to-equity (4.39x) arithmetically meaningless. At 24.8x FY2027 consensus — within two-tenths of a turn of Visa's multiple while growing faster — base fair value of $621 is 8.7% above spot. The better of the two networks to buy here, and still not cheap enough to buy today. Hold."

MAR.strategic_line: "Marriott reported yesterday and the shares are 14.2% below their 52-week high with a 14-day relative strength index of 33.7 — the most oversold reading in this batch — which is a strange place for a company that just beat consensus earnings by 3.6%. The 10-Q filed 2026-08-03 explains it. Worldwide comparable revenue per available room rose 3.4% in the June quarter, driven almost entirely by rate rather than occupancy, with the United States and Canada up 5.0% helped by World Cup demand in June 2026 — and INTERNATIONAL DOWN 0.5%, because the conflict in the Middle East produced what the company calls a sharp decline in RevPAR in our Middle East and Africa region beginning in March 2026, with the impact from the conflict continuing into the third quarter. The same war that doubled Marathon Petroleum's refining margin elsewhere in this batch is taking Marriott's international room rates down. Full-year net rooms growth is now guided toward the LOW END of the 4.5 to 5.0 percent range, revenue missed the estimate by 1.7%, United States and Canada segment profit FELL despite higher net fee revenues on a $68 million hotel impairment and a $27 million litigation accrual, and the company has bought back $2.2 billion of stock in seven months — more than its entire first-half operating cash flow of $1,806 million — funding the gap with debt and leaving shareholders' equity at MINUS $3,771 million. At $345.20 the stock is 29.6x the FY2026 consensus of $11.67 and 26.5x FY2027's $13.05. Our base fair value of $370 is 7.2% above spot with 1.75:1 asymmetry: close to the Tactical bar and not over it. The knowledge base contains exactly one name-level claim and it is the relevant one — that Airbnb, also in this batch, threatens upper-scale and luxury players like Marriott and Hilton while leaving the economy and mid-scale tiers alone."

MCD.strategic_line: "This dive replaces an earlier 2026-08-04 MCD dive written against a truncated SEC archive that contained FIVE documents and only TWO 8-Ks. The complete archive contains six, and the two additions are both dated 2026-08-04 — the day of this dive — and are both material. FIRST: McDonald's reported second-quarter 2026 results this morning. Adjusted EPS of $3.38 beat the $3.32 consensus by 1.8%; revenue of $7,099 million MISSED the $7,128.7 million estimate by 0.4%. The stock rose 1.17% to $268.34. SECOND, and filed the same day: 'On August 3, 2026, Joseph M. Erlinger, Executive Vice President of McDonald's Corporation and President of McDonald's USA, provided notice to the Company of his intention to leave his current role, effective August 4, 2026' — one day's notice, effective immediately, on earnings day, from the executive running 40.3% of revenue. Skye Anderson, a 26-year company veteran and most recently Chief Operating Officer of McDonald's USA, was appointed the same day. Erlinger is also the only officer in the insider file, having exercised options at a $157.79 strike on 2026-06-10. Against that: the stock is 21.3% below its 52-week high and 2.1% above its 52-week LOW, down 11.4% over twelve months while the index rose 24.3%, trading at 19.1x the FY2027 consensus of $14.072 for a business with a 46.0% operating margin, $7,186 million of free cash flow on a filing-verified capital-expenditure line, and a 3.82% total shareholder yield. Base fair value $293, 9.2% above spot, asymmetry 2.03:1 — over the bar, and this is the closest call in the batch. It is Watch and not a Buy because the base upside is under 10%, because the highest-skill voice in our knowledge base is bearish on this exact name and has been right for a year, and because the head of the largest segment resigned this morning without a stated reason."

MCK.strategic_line: "McKesson earns 31.1% on invested capital distributing drugs at a 3.6% gross margin, and the market has spent nine months deciding it does not care. The stock is $830.43 — 16.6% below its 52-week high, 0.7% BELOW its 200-day average, up 18.8% over twelve months against SPY's 24.3% and DOWN 1.9% over six. Meanwhile fiscal 2026 (ended 2026-03-31) delivered revenue of $403,430 million (+12.4%), adjusted earnings of $39.15 per share against a $39.01 consensus, GAAP diluted EPS of $38.38 against $25.72 a year earlier, and $4.8 billion of share repurchase — 4.9% of the market capitalisation in one year. Consensus wants $44.26 in FY2027 and $50.42 in FY2028, 13.4% then 13.9% growth, putting the stock at 18.8x and 16.5x. And there is a real corporate event in flight that no screen captures: McKesson has announced its intention to separate the entire Medical-Surgical Solutions segment into an independent company, has signed Apollo Funds to take a ~13% minority interest for ~$1.25 billion of convertible preferred, and on 9 June 2026 put a $2,250 million senior secured Term B loan due 2032 into the subsidiary holdco. None of that is in the vendor payload. Our base fair value of $930 is 12.0% above spot with 2.0:1 asymmetry, against a street consensus of $1,006 we are deliberately 7.6% below. THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS TIMING: McKesson reports first-quarter fiscal 2027 results TOMORROW, 5 August 2026, and this verdict is written with that as an explicit input — the position is not to be established before the print. The counterweights are named: stockholders' equity is NEGATIVE $2,172 million so every book-based ratio in the file is void; CVS alone is 24% of revenue and the top ten customers are 73%; opioid litigation is permanent; the vendor understates fiscal 2026 capital expenditure by $309 million of capitalised software; and the entire knowledge-base lane is three claims from ONE voice."

MCO.strategic_line: "Moody's is one of the two best businesses in this batch and it is priced as such. The June quarter grew revenue 15.1% and operating income 24.1%, on a 45.1% trailing operating margin and a 23.9% return on invested capital, from a company that rates roughly 40% of the world's debt and whose knowledge-base lane — five claims, every one bullish, convictions of 70 to 85 — describes an 'unassailable protocol-network-effect moat' that makes it 'ownable for 30+ years'. The problem is that the reported earnings jump is not what it appears. Diluted EPS of $5.02 against $3.20 is +56.9%, and the 10-Q states that the increase 'reflects growth in operating income coupled with the gain on the divestiture of the MA Regulatory Solutions business'. Below the operating line, the residual between operating income and pre-tax income swung from MINUS $24 million to PLUS $192 million year on year — a $216 million favourable swing the filing attributes principally to that divestiture, which appears in no vendor field. On operating income alone the quarter grew 24.1%, and that is the number to use. At $483.67 the shares are 25.6x the FY2027 consensus of $18.90 — a PEG near 2.2 on 11.7% forecast EPS growth. Our base fair value of $491 is 1.6% above spot with 1.09:1 asymmetry. Two data findings: `seg_geo` reports a line labelled 'U S' of $472 million against actual United States revenue of roughly $4,171 million, because the block carries an 'International Regions' aggregate of $3,547 million alongside its own components and has mislabelled the residual; and the trailing capital-expenditure figure implies roughly $83 million against $326 million filed for FY2025 — a 75% collapse that trips the below-15%-of-depreciation screen and cannot be checked, because the Moody's filing extraction is prose-only."

MDB.verdict: Hold — the highest-conviction knowledge-base lane in this batch (no_priors at conviction 85, all_in at 75 and 80) sits on a business that is genuinely accelerating, with revenue growth moving from 19% to 25% year over year, free cash flow inflecting from $121M to $500M, and $2.35B of net cash. But at 58.5x FY27 consensus non-GAAP earnings with stock compensation at 22.3% of revenue and GAAP operating income still negative, our base fair value of $400 lands exactly on the street consensus of $400.18. No variant perception on price means no edge. Own the business on weakness below $300; do not add here.
MDB.strategic_line: MongoDB is the rare name where the panel and the numbers agree and the price is the only obstacle, and we say so rather than manufacture a reason to buy. The business case is strong and improving in a way that is easy to verify: Atlas, the managed cloud database, grew from $1.405B to $1.808B — 28.6% — and is now 73.4% of revenue, and total revenue growth has ACCELERATED across four quarters from 18.7% to 23.7% to 26.8% to 25.2%, which is the opposite of what happens to infrastructure software that is losing relevance. GAAP operating loss narrowed from $233.7M (FY24) to $216.1M (FY25) to $137.0M (FY26), and free cash flow more than quadrupled to $500.2M. Net cash is $2.35B against $32.9M of debt. Our own knowledge base carries the best statement of the thesis: no_priors, January 2026, at conviction 85 — MongoDB is the only truly disruptive database force past $2B, with a large durable market, mission-critical sticky applications, and a strong position for AI-native unstructured data. That is a real lane and it underwrites owning this company. What it does not underwrite is paying 58.5 times next year's adjusted earnings for it. Stock-based compensation is $550.5M — 22.3% of revenue and MORE than the entire free cash flow — which means the non-GAAP earnings the multiple is calculated on exclude a cost larger than the cash the business produces. Strip that out and the GAAP business still loses money. Our base case of $400 is derived by holding roughly today's forward multiple and rolling it one year, and it lands within half a percent of the street's $400.18 consensus target. When our number equals the crowd's number, the honest label is Hold. The company deserves ownership; this price does not deserve new capital.

MDGL.strategic_line: A one-drug MASH launch priced at ~11× sales — it gets interesting below ~$470 (200-DMA zone, ~25% margin of safety to our base case); a second sequential revenue decline or visible GLP-1 share loss breaks the thesis.

MDLN.verdict: Watch — a genuine deleveraging-driven earnings engine sitting behind a compressing gross margin, an $800M sponsor sale at 10% below today's price with roughly 100 million shares still to come, and an earnings print tomorrow. Our base case is $41 against a $40.47 spot — no margin of safety at all. The interest-expense reduction is real and underappreciated ($233M per quarter to $165M in twelve months), but with gross margin down 220 basis points year-over-year, zero segment disclosure, no 200-day average, a corrupted beta and zero knowledge-base coverage, this is not a name to initiate seven months after its IPO.
MDLN.strategic_line: Medline is a $29 billion-revenue medical-surgical manufacturer and distributor that came public on 2025-12-17 out of a private-equity ownership structure, and it should be read as a post-buyout deleveraging story rather than as a growth story. The deleveraging is the underappreciated fact: net debt fell from $16,649M (FY24) to $10,622M (FY25) — a $6,027M reduction funded by the offering — and quarterly interest expense has fallen from $233M (June 2025) to $165M (March 2026), a 29% reduction worth roughly $270M a year flowing straight to pre-tax income on a business that earned $964M of trailing net income. That alone is a meaningful earnings tailwind and it is mechanical rather than operational. Revenue growth is respectable and consistent for the scale: $23,231M (FY23) to $25,507M (FY24, +9.8%) to $28,432M (FY25, +11.5%), with the March quarter up 10.7% year-over-year. But three things stop this being buyable. Gross margin fell from 24.8% in the March 2025 quarter to 22.6% in the March 2026 quarter — 220 basis points on a business with a 6-7% operating margin, which is a large proportion of the profit pool — while GAAP net income for the same quarter fell from $322M to $129M even as the adjusted figure beat. A ten-percent owner sold 21,969,126 shares at $36.5375 on 2026-05-28, roughly $803M, at a price 9.7% below today's, and retains approximately 99.8 million shares — about 12% of the count — as a continuing overhang. And the file offers no segment revenue at all, no geographic revenue at all, no 200-day moving average, no twelve-month return, and a reported beta of negative 0.41. Base case $41 against a $40.47 spot with earnings tomorrow. Watch.

MDLZ.strategic_line: "Mondelez reported a June quarter in which GAAP diluted earnings per share rose 144.9% to $1.20 and adjusted earnings per share were FLAT at $0.73 — and the entire difference is mark-to-market on commodity and currency derivatives, which the company says outright drove operating margin from 13.0% to 20.8% while ADJUSTED operating margin fell from 14.3% to 13.1%. The vendor payload carries the GAAP series and nothing else, which means every quarterly margin, every EBITDA figure and every earnings comparison in it is a cocoa-hedge artefact. Underneath the accounting, organic net revenue grew 2.2% in the quarter and 2.6% in the half, adjusted earnings per share fell 8.8% on a constant-currency basis in the half, and Europe chocolate volumes are still declining after last year's pricing. The company's response has been to raise the dividend 4% to $0.52 and to cut the buyback by roughly 91% — $210 million of repurchase in the first half against $2,385 million in all of fiscal 2025. All six filings in this archive are PROSE-ONLY with zero surviving tables, so the balance sheet cannot be reconciled; what can be reconciled is capital expenditure, which the management discussion states in prose and which matches the payload to the dollar in all three years. At $62.08 that is 20.4x the 2026 consensus, and the consensus needs a fourth quarter 29% above last year's to get there. Our base of $65 is 4.7% above spot. The knowledge base holds no claim naming this company and a genuinely relevant category lane — GLP-1s, ultra-processed food, and a three-way disagreement about cocoa — that we quote at zero weight."

MDT.strategic_line: "Medtronic has spent a decade being the medical-device company that did not grow, and fiscal 2026 is the first year in a long time where that is measurably untrue. Revenue rose 8.4% to $36,364 million against a four-year compound rate of 3.5%, and the 10-K names the drivers at product level rather than in aggregate: Cardiac Rhythm and Heart Failure net sales rose 17% on 'strong growth in the pulsed ablation portfolio', Structural Heart and Aortic rose 7%, Coronary and Peripheral Vascular rose 5% on the Symplicity Spyral renal denervation system, and Diabetes rose 13%. Quarterly year-on-year growth across fiscal 2026 was +8.4%, +6.6%, +8.8% and +9.9% — accelerating through the year — with five consecutive earnings beats. And on 9 March 2026 the Diabetes business completed an initial public offering as MiniMed Group, with roughly 10% sold and Medtronic retaining approximately 90%, an event that appears in no vendor field and that removes the segment the knowledge base's only claim on this company says is structurally disadvantaged. Against that: a 6.13% return on invested capital that is the honest indictment of thirty years of acquisition, 56.7% of assets in goodwill and intangibles, 2.68x net leverage, filings in this archive that are PROSE-ONLY so no statement table is verifiable, and a `seg_geo` block reporting United States revenue of $71,397 million for a company with $36,364 million of total revenue. At $86.20 the stock trades at 14.5x the FY2027 consensus against medical-device peers at well over twenty, 18.2% below its 52-week high and 36.2% below its multi-year peak, with 31 buy ratings and ZERO sells. Our base of $100 is 16.0% above spot; with the 3.31% dividend the total is 19.3%, against a bear case 13.0% down. That asymmetry is the best in this batch and it is arithmetic, not narrative."

MELI.strategic_line: "MercadoLibre is growing revenue faster than any other company in this batch and its earnings have stopped growing. March-quarter revenue was $8,845 million, up 49.0% year on year, while operating income FELL 19.9% to $611 million and net income fell 15.6% to $417 million — an operating margin of 6.9% against 12.9% a year earlier. Consensus expects FY2026 adjusted EPS of $39.34 against the $39.40 the company actually delivered in 2025: flat, on revenue up roughly 41%. That is either the Amazon-style investment mode the knowledge base describes — seven claims, every one bullish, on logistics capex building a moat and a credit book whose net interest margin after losses is rising — or it is competitive spend that does not stop. The market has voted: the stock is down 20.5% over twelve months against SPY's plus 24.3%, 24.8% below its 52-week high, and it has MISSED consensus in four consecutive quarters, by 13.6%, 8.8%, 3.7% and 5.9%. It reports again TOMORROW, 5 August, against $8.67 and $9,742 million. At $1,888.50 the shares are 49.8x trailing adjusted earnings, 48.0x FY2026 consensus and 33.5x FY2027's $56.318 — and that FY2027 number requires 43.1% growth immediately after a flat year, which makes it the load-bearing and least-supported assumption in the price. Our base fair value of $2,140 is 13.3% above spot with 2.35:1 asymmetry; the street's $2,166.67 is 14.7% above. Two data findings: the vendor's 11.18% free-cash-flow yield includes Mercado Pago's customer float and credit-book funding, which the company's own 10-Q explicitly strips out of its adjusted free cash flow; and the 212-day receivable cycle is a loan book, not a trade balance. Both `seg_prod` and `seg_geo` reconcile to the dollar, which is rare and is recorded."

META.strategic_line: "Meta is the deepest drawdown in this batch and the clearest contrarian set-up: $587.94, DOWN 25.6% from the 52-week closing high of $790.00, only 11.8% above the low, below both moving averages, with an RSI of 26.2 and a twelve-month return of MINUS 21.6% against the S&P's PLUS 24.3% — a 46-point deficit. The whole analyst target band, from a low of $595 to a high of $883, sits above the price. Two quarters of headline earnings are both distorted and neither means what it looks like. The Q1 blowout — EPS $10.44 against a $6.70 estimate — was mostly a DISCRETE INCOME TAX BENEFIT OF $8.03 BILLION from transitional relief, worth about $3.13 a share; strip it and the beat was $0.61. The Q2 miss on 2026-07-29 — EPS $6.18 against $7.19 — was not Reality Labs, whose loss rose only $89 million: it was the Family of Apps, whose income from operations FELL 6% while its revenue ROSE 28%, on infrastructure, legal costs, third-party compute and $1.18 billion of severance for a headcount reduction of approximately 8,000. Clean trailing earnings are about $29.61 against a reported $26.54, so the stock is on roughly 19.9x trailing and 17.1x FY2027 consensus. The de-rating is rational and the filings say why. In seven months, uncommenced lease obligations went from $103.77B to $278.99B, plus $68B more signed in July 2026; non-cancelable contractual commitments went from $131.05B to $349.31B; 2026 capital-expenditure guidance was raised from $115-135B to $130-145B; and Meta REPURCHASED NO STOCK AT ALL in the first half of 2026 after $26.26B in 2025. Free cash flow was $46.109B in 2025 and is heading toward roughly nothing. The balance sheet, however, is not the problem the vendor claims: net debt is $2.305B, not the $48.024B reported, because the file discards $45.719B of marketable securities. Base fair value $690, 17.4% above spot and below the street. Buy the fear in tranches; the answer arrives on 28 October."

MMM.strategic_line: "3M has beaten consensus in five consecutive quarters, lifted trailing adjusted earnings to $8.56, repurchased $4,813 million of stock in fiscal 2025 — 5.1% of the company in one year — and pays a 1.66% dividend, giving a total shareholder yield near 6.8% that is the second-highest in this programme. William Brown's operational turnaround is visibly working: June-quarter revenue of $6,500 million beat by 1.6% and adjusted EPS of $2.40 beat by 6.7%. The market has noticed. The stock rose 2.38% today to $181.45, is 28.2% above its 52-week low, has risen 28.2% in three months against SPY's 7.6%, carries an RSI of 75.3 — the most overbought reading in this batch — and sits 0.56% below its 52-week high with a maximum twelve-month drawdown of 0.56%. The vendor's consensus price target is $185, which is 2.0% above spot. Our base fair value of $186 is 2.5% above spot with 1.32:1 asymmetry. That is a Hold, and the dividend and buyback are the reason to keep owning it rather than the price. Underneath sits a liability that has no terminal value in any model: 3M completed its exit from PFAS manufacturing at the end of 2025 and divested Dyneon GmbH in June 2026, but the 10-Q states that 3M Deutschland 'remains responsible for PFAS-related claims arising from activities conducted prior to the divestiture,' that regulatory limits are 'being established at progressively lower levels, in some cases approaching limits that exceed current analytical detection capabilities,' and that proposed legislation 'may authorize recovery of healthcare or related public costs.' Free cash flow was $1,396 million against $3,250 million of net income. The knowledge base returned thirty-two hits and every one is noise — '$3M', '3mm', 'MMM' inside other strings — the largest total-noise sweep in this batch."

MNST.strategic_line: "Monster Beverage is a very good business at a price that already says so, reporting earnings in two days and splitting its stock in six. The March 2026 quarter was the best organic acceleration in the company's recent record — net sales of $2,353.3 million, up 26.9% year on year and up 22.1% adjusted for currency, with operating margin rising to 31.0% from 30.7% and gross margin at 55.8% for the full prior year against 54.0% the year before, driven by pricing actions and supply-chain optimisation. The balance sheet carries zero debt, $2,765.1 million of cash and short-term investments plus $487.3 million of long-term investments, a 25.5% return on equity and a 21.9% return on invested capital. And the stock trades at 45.3x trailing earnings, 40.9x the FY2026 consensus of $2.30 and 36.2x FY2027's $2.60 for consensus EPS growth of 13.1% — a forward PEG the vendor computes at 3.46. Our base fair value of $95 is 0.9% above the $94.18 close; the street's consensus target of $96.27 is 2.2% above it, despite 23 of 44 analysts carrying a Buy rating, which is a disconnect worth naming. Two corporate actions are absent from the vendor payload and both are found in the 8-K record: a 2-for-1 stock split declared 2026-07-08, record date 2026-07-24, distributed after the close on 2026-08-10 with split-adjusted trading from 2026-08-11 — six days after this dive, and every price, per-share and estimate figure in the payload is pre-split; and a new $500.0 million repurchase authorisation approved 2026-05-14 on top of approximately $400.0 million remaining. The knowledge-base sweep returned 54 raw hits and exactly one that names the company, with 'Celsius' collapsing entirely into Celsius Network, the failed crypto lender, rather than the energy-drink competitor — a textbook homograph collapse, reported as a discarded sweep."

MO.strategic_line: "Altria is the arithmetic of managed decline, and the arithmetic still works — but the vendor file describes a company growing 15% a year, and it is growing 0.1%. In the June 2026 quarter net revenues were $6,111 million against $6,102 million a year earlier, up 0.1%, and revenues net of excise taxes were $5,392 million against $5,357 million, up 0.7%. The vendor's `inc_q` block shows $6,111 million against $5,290 million — plus 15.5% — because it reports the 2026 quarters on the gross NET REVENUES basis and the 2025 quarters on the REVENUES NET OF EXCISE TAXES basis. Two different lines from the same income statement, compared to each other. Underneath, the 10-Q is candid: inventory-adjusted domestic cigarette shipment volume fell 4.5% against an industry down 5%; the discount share of the cigarette category reached 33.8%, up 2.6 points in a year, as consumers trade down; and the US nicotine pouch category grew to 59.9% of the oral tobacco market, up 8.1 points, which is Altria's moist-smokeless franchise being displaced by a competitor's product. Against that stands the cash: a 59.8% operating margin, capital expenditure of $216 million on $20.1 billion of revenue, $9,074 million of free cash flow, a 36.7% return on invested capital, and a $4.24 dividend yielding 6.23% that consumed 77% of free cash flow. At $68.07 the stock is 12.26x trailing adjusted earnings and 11.6x the 2027 consensus, and the total-return arithmetic is a 6.23% yield plus roughly 4% earnings growth. Our base of $73 is 7.2% above spot and within a dollar of the street's $72.33. The knowledge base names Altria exactly zero times. Watch."
